historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term revenue growth after the FY2026 guidance year, anchored to the FY2019->FY2025 pre-COVID-based revenue CAGR of 3.8% and Boeing-constrained capacity; the equity and EPS CAGRs are negative and cannot anchor a growth path
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-9.3% 3yr) and EPS CAGR (-3.4% 3yr) diverge by far more than 30% from revenue (+5.6% 3yr): equity shrank through $3.8B of buybacks in FY2025-H1 2026 funded from the post-COVID cash pile, and EPS collapsed on the labor reset and transformation costs. The 5-year revenue CAGR (25.4%) is a FY2020 COVID-trough artefact and is not a trend. Growth is anchored to revenue and to management guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), $M: FY2019 2,815; FY2020 -1,691; FY2021 1,746; FY2022 -435; FY2023 -1,025; FY2024 -2,134; FY2025 -1,135. Reported FCF for the same years: 2,960; -1,642; 1,817; -134; -356; -1,592; -831. The owner adjustment is $0.6-1.1B/yr in FY2023-FY2025, almost all of it interest income on the $9-13B post-COVID cash pile, not SBC (SBC is 0.3-0.4% of revenue). Both FCF CAGRs are null because the endpoints are negative; the business has not produced positive owner FCF since FY2021, which is the whole reason this build is normalized rather than extrapolated. H1-2026 reported FCF is +$499M (OCF 1,947 less capex 1,448), the first positive half-year since H1-2023.

scenario_narratives.base: Base: partial transformation success. FY2026 revenue +14% (H1 +14.7% actual, Q3 RASM guide +17.5-19.5%) at a 12.5% EBITDA margin that splits the difference between the GAAP run-rate and the adjusted-guidance midpoint; margin ramps 1pp a year to a 15.5% mid-cycle level by FY2030 as the >$1B cost program and premium/loyalty mix land against higher labor and a normalizing fuel bill. Growth decelerates 5% -> 2.5% because Boeing constrains capacity. Capex 9-9.5% of revenue through FY2028 then 8%; cash tax ramps 10% -> 23%. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF (~4x EBITDA), so no re-rating is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Bull: the plan delivers. Unit revenue reaches legacy-peer parity through assigned/extra-legroom seating, premium card and lounges and managed-business share; cost takeout sticks; Boeing recovers so capacity grows 4-6% on more efficient MAX 7/8s. EBITDA margin 18% by FY2030 (management's 2027 EBIT ambition, two to three years late), still below the 2015-2017 peak. Same WACC and same 12x cap: the upside is in the flows, not in a cheaper discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: Bear: cost savings land but revenue gains are competed away and brand goodwill erodes; route exits cede share; fuel stays high; FY2026 closes at the low end of the cut guidance. EBITDA margin stuck at 11.5-12%, revenue growth 1.5-2%, terminal growth 2%. The balance sheet survives (net debt ~0.5x EBITDA, $3.8B cash, $2.15B 2027 maturities refinanceable) so this is a value-destruction case, not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Southwest is valued as a cyclical operating company on a normalized owner-FCF basis: the trailing FCF is negative and meaningless, management's 2027 targets are an ambition, and the base case sits deliberately between them at a 15.5% mid-cycle EBITDA margin reached in FY2030. The owner-FCF margin that results (4-5% of revenue) is thin because an airline must reinvest 2-4% of revenue above D&A to keep its fleet, which is why the equity is worth roughly 11-12x normalized owner FCF and ~4-5x EBITDA at the terminal, not a compounder multiple. Risk is charged once, in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights, at a single 9.5% USD WACC. The house and street bases nearly coincide because SBC is 0.35% of revenue; the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2026 EBITDA margin: GAAP H1 run-rate ~9% vs ~13% implied by adjusted guidance; the base uses 12.5%. Each 1pp of year-1 margin is ~$320M of EBITDA.

Mature margin level: 15.5% base vs 12% bear vs 18% bull is the dominant driver of the per-share spread; the FY2015-FY2019 18.6-25.9% range is not used as a reference because it rested on sub-$2 fuel and pre-2024 labor rates.
Capex intensity: fleet renewal when Boeing recovers could run above 9.5% of revenue for longer; every 1pp of capex-to-revenue in perpetuity is roughly $5/share.

Terminal cap at 12x owner FCF (~4x EBITDA) is conservative against today's ~5.5x EV/EBITDA; a reader who believes the market pays 6x EBITDA for a transformed Southwest should read the Gordon value in the sensitivity grid.
Cash tax ramp: bonus depreciation on a delivery catch-up could keep cash taxes below the 23% assumed from year 5, which would add value; a faster unwind would subtract it.

Fuel and macro: a leisure-skewed airline with large unhedged fuel exposure; a recession in the 10-year window is likely and is represented by the 25% bear weight rather than by a cyclical dip in the base path.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 29.26-55.11.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts CIK 0000092380: 10-K FY2025 (revenue, D&A, SBC, interest income, cash taxes, leases, buybacks) and 10-Q Q2 2026 (debt split, cash, diluted shares, cover-page share count at 2026-07-22); research/LUV/Reports/LUV_Metrics.csv for the FY2007-H1 2026 history.
data_sources.qualitative: research/LUV/Reports/LUV_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q2 2026 results and guidance cut, assigned-seating rollout, Boeing delivery shortfall, cost program, Elliott stake reduction, route cuts.

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 489.2M cover-page shares at 2026-07-22 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, Q2 2026 10-Q) + ~4M dilutive RSUs (IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements Q2 2026) = 493M, which also equals the Q2 2026 diluted weighted average. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The 2025 convertible notes matured May 2025, so no conversion dilution remains.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense = $99M (cash-flow add-back basis). Southwest publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure and tags no separate net-share-settlement withholding; RSU withholding is immaterial at this SBC scale (0.35% of revenue), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $2,550M (ASRs), plus $1,250M in Q1 2026 and $0 in Q2 2026. The flat share count is more than funded: the count fell 643M -> 493M diluted in 18 months. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; their cash cost is why net debt swung from net cash to +$2.2B.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x airline beta ~1.3 = cost of equity ~10.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (new 2026 notes ~5.5-6% pre-tax); market-value weights ~80/20 equity/debt (market cap ~$20.6B vs debt $5.9B) -> WACC ~9.4%, rounded to 9.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, fuel, Boeing and transformation-execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and the probability weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost, as US GAAP ASC 842 already does for operating leases: FY2025 LeaseCost $2,529M (of which $2,130M variable airport charges, $346M fixed operating-lease payments) sits inside operating expense, so it is inside every EBITDA margin in this model and inside reported OCF. Operating lease liabilities ($943M at 2026-06-30: 283 current + 660 non-current) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial ($78M at FY2025) and sit inside total_debt, with their $22M/yr principal treated as debt service. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed because nothing is being moved out of EBITDA.
inputs.debt_note: total_debt $5,946M at 2026-06-30 = LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations non-current $3,790M + current $2,156M (Q2 2026 10-Q), the current portion being the $2,150M of notes maturing in 2027 reclassified. Includes ~$70M of finance leases. $1.5B of new notes issued in H1 2026 ($1.0B in Q2) is in this figure. Cash $3,791M, short-term investments $0 (sold down during 2025; PaymentsToAcquireShortTermInvestments 0 in H1 2026). NOTE for the parser: the DB's FY2025 total_debt of 5,253 double-counts the $324M current portion (LongTermDebt 4,929 already includes it; the filed LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsIncludingCurrentMaturities is 4,919); the Q2 2026 figure used here reconciles exactly to the filing and is not affected.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, mid-cycle/normalized basis (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of LUV; no memory entry. WHY NOT TRAILING FCF: FY2025 owner FCF is -$1,135M (reported -$831M less $99M SBC less $205M interest income) and FY2022-FY2025 owner FCF was negative every year, because post-COVID the business ran 7-10% GAAP EBITDA margins against 7.5-16.5% capex-to-revenue during fleet renewal and the labor reset (pilots +29% initial, flight attendants). Extrapolating that yields a negative value for a business guiding to $3.25-4.25 adjusted EPS this year; extrapolating management's 2027 EBIT ambition yields a value no buyer has to grant. The base case therefore normalizes: EBITDA margin ramps from 12.5% in FY2026 (between the ~9-10% GAAP H1-2026 run-rate and the ~13% implied by the midpoint of adjusted EPS guidance, because a share of the special items - severance, contract items, restructuring - are real cash costs during the transformation) to a 15.5% mature level by FY2030 and holds. 15.5% is below the FY2015-FY2019 fuel-tailwind, pre-labor-reset peak (18.6-25.9%), well above the FY2022-FY2025 trough (7-10%), in line with where Delta/United run post-labor-reset, and implies roughly half to two-thirds of management's $4B incremental-EBIT ambition lands. REVENUE: year 1 (FY2026) +14% from H1 +14.7% actual, Q3 RASM guidance +17.5-19.5% on roughly flat capacity, and Q4 lapping the May-2025 bag-fee launch; then 5% decelerating to 2.5% because Boeing is delivering 66 vs 167 committed MAX aircraft in 2026 and MAX 7 service does not start before Q1 2027, so capacity growth is constrained and growth must come from unit revenue. CAPEX: 9.0-9.5% of revenue through FY2028 (H1-2026 actual $1,448M annualizes to ~9% and deliveries catch up when Boeing recovers), tapering to 8.0% long run against D&A rising 5.2% -> 5.8%; net investment of 2-4% of revenue is what a fleet-renewing airline costs and is the main reason owner-FCF margins stay at 4-5% even at a 15.5% EBITDA margin. CASH TAX: FY2024-FY2025 net cash taxes were refunds (-$21M, -$1M) against ~22% GAAP provisions, driven by accelerated/bonus depreciation on deliveries; ramped 10% -> 23% statutory-equivalent by year 5 as the deferral unwinds, never credited on a loss. WORKING CAPITAL: positive 10% capture of the revenue change because air traffic liability ($8.2B, ~26% of revenue) grows with bookings and dwarfs receivables. INTEREST INCOME: $205M FY2025 stripped from last_fcf for consistency with the unlevered forward build; the cash it was earned on ($3.8B) is in the net-debt bridge, and the pile has largely been spent on buybacks since (FY2026 run-rate ~$110M). TERMINAL: Gordon at 2.5% growth vs a 12x owner-FCF cap (cyclical rule); the cap binds in every scenario and implies ~4x terminal EV/EBITDA, below today's ~5.5x, so the model assumes no re-rating. HORIZON: 10 years because the margin is still ramping at year 5 under a 5-year build. The special-items gap between GAAP and adjusted EBITDA (~$300M pre-tax in Q2 2026 alone) is the single biggest near-term judgment; if FY2026 closes at the adjusted-guidance EBITDA with no cash leakage, year 1 is ~0.5-1pp of margin light.

bear.narrative: The transformation delivers the cost side but the revenue gains are competed away: customers who flew Southwest for free bags and open seating defect to ULCCs on price and to Delta/United on product, route exits (68 routes cut for Q3 2026) cede share permanently, fuel stays elevated, and FY2026 closes near the low end of the cut guidance. EBITDA margin stalls at 11.5-12%, the level the GAAP run-rate already implies, with revenue growth of 1.5-2% as Boeing shortfalls persist. Capex still has to fund fleet replacement at 7.5-9% of revenue, so owner FCF stays thin.

base.narrative: Transformation lands partially. Assigned seating, bag fees and fare tiers close roughly half of the unit-revenue gap to legacy peers; the cost program delivers its >$1B run-rate by 2027 but a share is reinvested in labor and premium product; Boeing deliveries normalize from 2027-2028 so capex runs 9-9.5% of revenue before settling at 8%. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin of 15.5% reached FY2030 and held, below the 2015-2019 cheap-fuel peak and in line with post-labor-reset legacy peers.

bull.narrative: The 'Southwest. Even Better.' plan broadly delivers: assigned/extra-legroom seating, premium card and lounges, and managed-business share (+30% YoY in Q2 2026) lift unit revenue to legacy-carrier parity; >$1B of structural cost comes out and sticks; MAX 7 enters service Q1 2027 and Boeing catches up, so capacity growth returns to 4-6% with better fuel burn. EBITDA margin reaches 18% by FY2030, close to management's 2027 EBIT ambition on a slower timetable and still below the 2015-2017 cheap-fuel peak.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot - the company is dismantling the two differentiators (free bags, open seating) that built its brand, FY2026 guidance was just cut and Q3 guided below consensus, and airlines are the most cyclical business in the folder. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: customer acceptance of the new model, the cost program sticking, Boeing recovering, and fuel cooperating. Base 50%: H1 2026 record revenue and real margin expansion say the transformation is working, just more slowly and less completely than management's 2027 framework.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
